title: Calculate Digit Sum of a String
statement:
You get a string of digits `s` and an integer `k`. While `s` is longer than `k` characters, perform a round:

1. Cut `s` from left to right into pieces of `k` characters each; only the final piece may be shorter.
2. Swap every piece for the decimal form of the sum of its digits (for instance `"346"` turns into `"13"`, since 3 + 4 + 6 = 13).
3. Join the new pieces in their original order; the result is the new `s`.

Once `s` has at most `k` characters, no more rounds happen. Return the final `s`.
notes:
## Intuition

The rules describe a process, so the most direct solution is to carry it out exactly. Each round replaces up to `k` digits by a number of at most `9k`, which never has more digits than the piece it replaces when `k >= 2`, and the digit values shrink, so the loop always ends. With at most 100 characters, simulating every round is cheap.

## Approach

1. While `s` is longer than `k`, build the next string `next` from empty.
2. Step `start` through `s` in jumps of `k`; each piece ends at `end`, capped at the string's length so the last piece may be short.
3. Add the piece's digits into `groupSum` and append its decimal text to `next`.
4. Replace `s` with `next` and test the length again.
5. When `s` fits in `k` characters, return it.

## Example 1, step by step

`s = "11111222223"`, `k = 3`. The length 11 exceeds 3, so the pieces are `"111"`, `"112"`, `"222"`, `"23"` with sums 3, 4, 6, 5, and `s` becomes `"3465"`. Its length 4 still exceeds 3: the pieces `"346"` and `"5"` sum to 13 and 5, so `s` becomes `"135"`. Now the length is 3, the loop stops, and `"135"` is returned.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n) per round for n characters; the string shrinks fast enough that 100 digits need only about a dozen rounds even with `k = 2`.
- Space: O(n) for the next string.

## Pitfalls

- Stop when the length is less than or equal to `k`, not only when it is smaller: `"000"` with `k = 3` is final.
- A sum can have several digits (`"99"` becomes `"18"`), so append its full decimal text, not a single character.
- Zero sums still write `"0"`; dropping them would shorten the string wrongly.
- Do not forget the final short piece when the length is not a multiple of `k`.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `s` | the current string, replaced after every round |
| `next` | the string being built for the next round |
| `start`, `end` | first index and one past the last index of the current piece |
| `groupSum` | sum of the digits in the current piece |
| `i` | index of the digit being added |

narration.2: A round happens only while the string is longer than k.
narration.3: Start an empty string for the result of this round.
narration.4: Jump through the string one piece of k characters at a time.
narration.5: The last piece stops at the end of the string, so it may be shorter.
narration.6: Begin this piece's digit sum at zero.
narration.7: Visit every digit of the piece.
narration.8: Turn the character into its digit value and add it.
narration.10: Append the sum's decimal text, which may be more than one character.
narration.12: The joined sums become the string for the next check.
narration.14: The string now has at most k characters, so it is the answer.
